brief: Goldman's ROIC framework asks how much revenue the six US hyperscalers (Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, Oracle, SpaceX) need to earn a 15% return on Phase 2 (2026-27) AI capex of $1.73 trillion. The answer: $1.42 trillion in cumulative revenue over 2028-30, or $11.6 billion per gigawatt. Goldman's main evidence this is achievable is the cloud backlog ($1.69 trillion, up 152% year over year), which covers 59% of the requirement, though Alphabet's 78% coverage is the tightest. A sensitivity test puts the range at $0.9 to $1.9 trillion, and even a zero-return scenario still needs $920 billion just to cover depreciation and operating costs. The note excludes off-balance-sheet lease and SPV obligations, which run roughly $3 trillion more. Depreciation of $276 billion a year is 1.7 times the EBIT the assets must produce, so the economics depend heavily on Goldman's 5-year useful-life assumption for compute holding rather than a shorter 3-year cycle. Morgan Stanley's separate ROIC math (25-50%) broadly agrees if GPU and token prices hold, but token prices have since fallen to record lows. Phase 3 (2028-30, $4.14 trillion) is left unaddressed. Extending the same ratio, the author (not Goldman) estimates roughly $3.4 trillion more would be needed.
